newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul to keep 4.0 pct bank ownership limit-finmin.
newsitem.headline: Seoul to keep 4.0 pct bank ownership limit-finmin.

text.p: South Korea's Finance Ministry has decided to keep the individual ownership ceiling on banks at the current four percent, a senior ministry official said on Tuesday.

Earlier a presidential commission reviewing financial reform measures proposed expanding the ceiling to up to 10 percent under certain conditions to help beef up competitiveness of the nation's banking industry.
The decision is due to be officially announced later on Tuesday, said the official who declined to be identified.
Last week the ministry unveiled its final reform draft based on the recommendations from the Presidential Commission for Financial Reform.
The ministry's draft included a plan to merge the three existing watchdog bodies into a single organisation under control of the prime minister.
The idea sparked a storm of criticism from union workers at the Office of Bank Supervision, the Securities Supervisory Board and the Insurance Supervisory Board.
The unions vowed to walk out if the ministry did not repeal the draft.
Senior officials at the central Bank of Korea, to which the Office of Bank Supervision belongs, also demanded that the ministry's plan be scrapped and that a fresh debate be started.
